assumptions: All orders are in scope (no filter on order type or merchant).
The period is 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Oct 2026.
caveats: Part of this answer uses custom SQL written by the AI, outside the governed semantic layer. It was validated (read-only, governed views only, role filters applied) before running, but its logic has not been reviewed like the governed metrics.
Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Volume spike 18 Oct–31 Oct: attempt volume was +39% versus the usual level for those weekdays over 14 days. Real business events (sales) and data gaps both look like this; check before comparing totals across this period.

facts.text: There were 419,385 orders in October 2026, of which 10,865 needed more than one payment attempt.
The share of orders with more than one attempt was 2.59% (shown as 2.6% in the headline).
On 12 Oct, 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts); duplicates were removed in the clean view, keeping the first ingestion.
Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was +39% versus the usual level for those weekdays over 14 days.

response.headline: In October 2026, 2.6% of orders (10,865 of 419,385) needed more than one payment attempt to complete payment.
